title: Boot sequencer and Helm expressions for safe credential seeding and phased bootstrap
author: Aisha Gomez
description:
Motivation: Private installer runs occasionally race when bootstrapping credentials and seeding initial secrets in air-gapped or multi-network environments. This PR introduces a lightweight boot sequencer controller pattern and Helm expression helpers to express phased bootstrap stages and conditional credential seeding. The goal is to reduce cross-namespace contention during first-run operations, make credential seeding idempotent, and provide a readable values contract for operators.

What this PR does: - Adds a small, cluster-scoped "boot-sequencer" controller implemented as a Kubernetes Job template that is invoked via Helm hooks during install/upgrade for Private installs. The sequencer enforces namespace fanout and a configurable concurrency window. - Introduces Helm template helpers (templates/_boot_helpers.tpl) that expose functions: .Values.boot.sequenceProfile, .Values.boot.maxConcurrentNamespaces, and a new helm expression "maybeSeedCredentials" that gates seeding when KMS is available or when explicit override is set. - Values schema additions and layered defaults under values/boot-values.schema.yaml with examples for on-prem, VPC, and air-gapped installs. - Seed job template changes: the credential-seed Job now reads a SEED_POLICY env var generated by Helm expression; the job implements a built-in dry-run mode (--dry-run) toggled by values for safer upgrades. - Upgrade/rollback safety: a pre-upgrade hook ensures the sequencer drains outstanding bootstrap jobs before upgrade continues; rollback hook attempts a no-op reconcile and logs potential leftover artifacts.

Checklist: - [x] Add boot sequencer Job template and controller patterns - [x] Add Helm helpers and values schema - [x] Ensure credential-seed job is idempotent and supports dry-run - [x] Add integration test harness for sequential namespace seeding in perf-canary - [x] Update docs/installer/boot-sequencer.md - [x] Add release-note entry

Design notes and tradeoffs: The sequencer is intentionally lightweight (templated Job + leader-elector pattern using configmap lock) to avoid adding a long-lived controller binary to the private installer. That keeps the offline footprint small and avoids additional operator lifecycle. We accepted some templating complexity in Helm in exchange for making the flow explicit to operators (values-driven). For clusters with bespoke bootstrap tooling operators can disable the sequencer via values and run their own orchestration.

Rollback plan: The sequencer records namespace progress to a sequencer-status ConfigMap. On rollback we attempt to rehydrate that state and skip already-seeded namespaces. If a rollback can't safely determine seed state, operator guidance in docs instructs manual reconciliation steps.

Testing: Unit tests for Helm helpers, integration test in perf-canary that simulates 16 namespaces with maxConcurrentNamespaces=3, CI runs lint and schema validation. I ran an on-prem airgapped dry-run locally against a kind cluster and validated idempotent semantics.

Docs: docs/installer/boot-sequencer.md includes operator guidance, troubleshooting, and sample values for common deployment topologies.

review_comments: Liam Chen: Nice pattern, can we avoid cluster-scoped objects? Suggest switching to a namespaced ConfigMap with a stable name and leader-elector per-namespace.

Aisha Gomez: Replied: namespaced leader-elector was considered; we need cross-namespace visibility to enforce global concurrency window. I added a follow-up note in docs and made name collisions explicit for single-tenant installs.
Ravi Patel: Please add a short circuit when KMS is not configured to skip seeding and mark the namespace as SKIPPED. Also raise an alert if seed job fails >3 times.
Aisha Gomez: Replied: added maybeSeedCredentials helm expression and a SEED_RETRY_LIMIT variable; CI tests the backoff behavior.
Marina Lopez: Approved after a small nit — prefer a 30s jitter on job backoff instead of fixed 15s to avoid thundering herd.
Aisha Gomez: Updated: backoff jitter made configurable via values.boot.backoffJitterSeconds and tests updated.

release_notes: Add boot-sequencer and Helm helpers to orchestrate phased credential seeding during Private installs. Operators can configure sequence profiles, concurrency windows, and dry-run seeding. No breaking changes by default; sequencer is opt-in via values.
